data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"If the token budget is reserved per-event before the write begins\u2014each event write atomically reserves its cost from a global pool and releases unused reservation on completion\u2014then budget exhaustion never interrupts an in-progress write; it only prevents the next write from starting. Under this construction, all halts are clean by design, and resumption is always safe provided the reservation protocol was followed. Resumption must be refused only when the reservation protocol itself was violated: a write started without a successful reservation, or a reservation was held but no event was committed (leaving the budget in a locked state).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The per-event reservation protocol was not actually implemented or was bypassed (e.g., streaming output without pre-reservation), so a halt could still interrupt a write.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A reservation was deducted but the corresponding event was not committed (crash between reservation and write), leaving the budget artificially reduced relative to the event log.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The token-cost estimate is systematically wrong (e.g., output exceeds the estimate), so the reservation does not actually prevent mid-write exhaustion.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The reservation is per-event but non-deterministic external inputs are still un-logged, so even with a clean halt the continuation trajectory diverges.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Per-event budget reservation decouples exhaustion from write integrity. Before generating an event, the system estimates its token cost and atomically deducts that estimate from the budget. If insufficient budget remains, the write never starts\u2014the halt is at an event boundary by construction. If the actual cost is lower, the difference is returned; if higher, the event is still committed (the estimate was a floor). This collapses the clean-halt condition into normal operation: there is no 'interrupted write' state to guard against. The only corruption risk is if the reservation protocol fails (e.g., a write begins without reservation due to a bug, or a crash leaves a reservation locked without a committed event), creating a budget-event inconsistency. In that case, the append-only identity of existing events is intact, but the budget state is inconsistent, and resumption under a wrong budget could produce events that a continuous run would not have\u2014so refuse.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
